clues: He glances twice toward the dark alley behind the kiosk — not the bus stop.
He says he forgot his wallet — then says it again, word for word, like a line.
His hands tremble; the exhaustion looks lived-in, not performed.
A crumpled day-ticket stub sticks from his jacket — today's date, stamped, route from Piraeus.

stages.intro:
A man steps out of the metro mouth and catches your eye — round sunglasses, beaded necklace, the city night stuck to his skin.

"Hey — tourist? Please. I just need a few euros for the night bus. My card died. I can get home if I make the last one."
stages.ask: He waits, too close, palms half open.

walk_away.result:
You shake your head and turn.

He curses in a language you almost recognize. Footsteps follow for half a block, then stop.

You do not look back until the hotel lights.

stages.intro:
He rubs the tattoo at his throat like it itches when he talks.

"Shipyard work. Then nothing. Couch at my cousin's in Keratsini — if I make the bus. Miss it and I'm out here till morning with the dogs and the cops."

A thin laugh. "I know how I look. I used to hate guys like me too."
stages.ask: The last-bus clock in his head is louder than the square.

shut_it_down.result:
"I'm sorry. I can't."

He nods once, jaw tight, and drifts back toward the metro mouth.

You keep your hands in your pockets the whole way to the hotel.

stages.intro:
He stops under the stop's blue light and shows empty pockets like a bad magic trick.

"Three euros. That's it. Or walk me to the door of the bus so they don't think I'm hustling. I swear I'm not — not tonight."
stages.ask: The night bus is a rumor of headlights two corners away.

threat.text:
You dig out a note. He snatches it, pockets it, and — without breaking eye contact — lets rip a wet, theatrical fart aimed squarely at your shoes.

"Bus tip," he says, and walks off cackling.

You stand under the blue light smelling like a lost argument.

human.text:
He takes the note with both hands, almost laughing with relief.

"Thank you. Really. Get home safe."

He jogs toward the stop. For a moment the square feels less sharp.

threat.text:
You offer to walk him over. He thanks you, steers you past the fountain — into shadow.

The knife is already out. Heat, then cold, under your ribs.

Sirens somewhere. Then the square goes quiet.

human.text:
You walk him to the illuminated stop. He talks about missing the last train from Piraeus, about a cousin who leaves the key under a brick.

The night bus sighs open. He waves once from the steps.

You head back across the square feeling foolish — and safer.

refuse.result:
You keep your wallet shut.

"Okay," he says, smaller. "Okay."

He stays under the sign as you leave. Sleep comes late. The square stays in your ears.
